facts.fact: Le Soleil says Senegal's cybercrime law was promulgated on 25 January 2008 and governs the police Division speciale de cybersecurite.

Le Soleil reports Moustapha Diakhate was tried and sentenced on 28 November 2024 to two months in prison after a hearing at the Division speciale de cybersecurite for an insult committed through a computer system.
Le Soleil, citing the police 2024 annual report, says 3,902 of 18,951 offences were cybercrime complaints, of which 223 were cleared.

Le Soleil reports journalist Bachir Fofana was held from 25 June 2025, placed under committal and tried on 2 July 2025 for spreading false news, and commentator Badara Gadiaga was jailed from 14 July 2025 over remarks about Ousmane Sonko.

SEN.note: Describes a cybercrime police unit and complaint counts, not a station record system.
